# Bounded native program fixtures

`source.py` is copied unchanged from the r2 packet's
`probes/csd-r2/kernels.py`. Its original Idein MIT notice is retained in full.
These programs are integration-test inputs, not runtime special cases.

`programs.json` contains machine words regenerated with the r2 assembler
(`py-videocore7` revision `4707e67fcba62217293a5bb155bfd594d97d8eb3`). The
little-endian word hashes exactly match the recorded r2 native witness:

| Program | SHA256 of little-endian uint64 words |
| --- | --- |
| producer | `d5e53b29c7083edbcd1c24c852c7f77b083a3974b8a32f654bc9b0251338df3c` |
| consumer | `13cda0e576bebf439afc531e6e5ca57ffb358181606c4c1207c1fbdb0c807c98` |

The producer writes consecutive int32 values over 16 lanes per iteration. The
consumer reads and writes the same extent, adding one. The tested domain is
1–4096 iterations. The hardware runner uses 4096 and checks every output plus
guard regions and nonzero-offset views. Do not infer arbitrary kernel or shape
support from these witnesses.

The hardware test needs no Python assembler. To regenerate, supply a correctly
prepared checkout of the exact assembler revision (including its generated
version module), or the r2 `probes/csd-r2/qpu` tree:

```bash
python tools/generate_qpu_fixture.py \
  --assembler-root /absolute/path/to/r2/probes/csd-r2/qpu \
  --output /absolute/path/to/regenerated-programs.json
```

Compare all source, assembler, and machine-word hashes. Do not replace the
fixtures to accommodate a failing backend. The output JSON contains the exact
source and assembler hashes used here.

## Stage 2 copy fixture

`copy_source.py` and `copy_program.json` are a separately identified native
bit-preserving copy. The source retains the original MIT notice. It replaces
the read witness's integer increment with an exact word move, preserving the
same bounded TMU loop and launch ABI. The original `source.py` and
`programs.json` are unchanged.

Uniforms are iteration count, source address, and destination address; every
iteration copies 16 words. Admit 1–4096 iterations and identical or disjoint
ranges only. The program does not interpret FP32 values. The new target harness
first checks raw-bit preservation and guards independently, including NaN
payloads, signed zero, infinities, and a subnormal, before using this fixture
as the native producer/consumer around ggml.

The frozen new program has 24 64-bit words and SHA256
`45c3d5181a93c7cb448f7a569f6950917f4e608672e8090ce42405e0dd1fffd7`.
It was assembled on the authoring host, not run on Pi here. Its
`hardware_observed: false` is an immutable authoring claim; put new target
observations in receipts rather than editing that field to claim success.

To reproduce it with the pinned py-videocore7 package/check-out used for the
original witnesses:

```bash
python tools/generate_qpu_fixture.py --kind copy \
  --assembler-root /absolute/path/to/pinned/py-videocore7 \
  --output /absolute/path/to/run/copy_program-reassembled.json
```

The assembler hash is checked before importing it. Its normal Python package
metadata must be present/generated by its own packaging process; do not invent
`_version.py` to silence a broken package. The target test needs only the frozen
machine words and the new backend, not the old SDK/runtime environment.
